newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $0.50 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $0.50 - dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct hogs early Monday sold steady to $0.50 per cwt lower on continued soft pork demand and ongoing slaughter cutbacks, livestock dealers said.
At least one major packer in the interior Iowa and soutbern Minndesota area said it would continue running reduced shifts in an effort to improve operating margins.

Talk that several other plants also would maintain slaughter reductions that started a week ago, contributed to the weakness, dealers said. A slight increase in eastern Corn Belt hog marketings lent further pressure, sources there said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold steady, but could turn lower as the day progresses, with $56.00 to $57.00 paid in the country and $57.50 to $58.50 at plants.
Illinois hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower at $56.00 to $57.00 in the country and $57.50 to $58.00 at plants.

Indiana hogs sold $0.50 lower at $54.50 to $56.00 in the country and $57.00 to $58.00 at plants. Light rainfall Sunday was enough to stall fieldwork in parts of Indiana, which resulted in a few extra hogs sold early Monday, dealers said.
Ohio hogs sold steady at $54.00 to $55.00 in the country and $56.00 to $57.00 at plants, sources there said.
